html:
The Matsigenka are an Arawakan people of southeastern Peru, living in the high jungle on the eastern slopes of the Andes and in the Amazon lowlands, along the Urubamba and Manu rivers. About 18,000 people counted themselves Matsigenka in 2020.

In the 1400s they lived on the edge of the Inca Empire, trading forest goods such as feathers and cotton with the highlands. They were long hunter-gatherers and gardeners, growing manioc, maize and bananas in shifting plots. The rubber boom brought slave raids and violence to their rivers. Their kin the Asháninka live to the north. Today many Matsigenka live in settled communities and grow coffee and cacao for sale, while some small groups in the Manu forest still avoid contact. The Camisea gas project was built in their territory in the 2000s.
